mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increases weekday trip chains that spill into retail visits, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks as commuting normalizes.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days even while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both keep rising week over week.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stay deeply depressed, household substitution away from out-of-home activity weakens retail trips and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -35 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +8
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES remains below -35 and RESIDENTIAL remains above +8.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp jump in PARKS use reallocates discretionary time toward outdoor recreation, which temporarily competes with shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC down in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within one week of a PARKS increase exceeding 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to fall while TRANSIT remains weak, the snapshot reflects broad caution and compressed errand activity that should keep retail-and-recreation mobility below its recent level for four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -15 while TRANSIT stays below -45
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week mean during a period when GROCERY_PHARM stays below -15 and TRANSIT stays below -45.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS combined with only gradual improvement in other mobility channels signals seasonal outdoor substitution, which should hold retail mobility slightly lower over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite PARKS staying elevated and WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining depressed.

mechanism_narrative: A continued narrowing gap between RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES indicates more routine out-of-home activity and less home anchoring, which should lift retail visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week average even as RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT from very depressed levels is an early signal of easing movement constraints, and retail mobility should improve within two weeks if transit keeps recovering.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks after TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues improving while RETAIL_REC remains subdued, households are reallocating errands to necessities rather than discretionary shopping, so retail-and-recreation mobility should stay flat to lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC stays below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -30 within one week while GROCERY_PHARM continues improving.
